requirement:
If all callbacks return `Ok(_)` and any callback returns `Ok(VetResult::CorrectAndTryAgain(message))`, the answer is not recorded.

The harness collects the correction messages in registration order.
`submit_result` returns the newline-separated messages in one tool response
and asks the agent to resubmit in the same conversation.
rationale:
The test `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[vetting_collects_corrections_and_rechecks_every_callback]` covers each obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.vet_answer.corrections`. I did not read the implementation.

- **Answer not recorded when any callback returns `CorrectAndTryAgain`:** The first submission is `false`. Callback 2 rejects it and callback 3 corrects it, so neither can accept it. The final answer is `true` and `seen == [false, true]`. A recorded `false` would have ended the call with `false`, so the test would catch that.
- **All callbacks run on each round, with no short-circuit:** In round 1, callback 2 returns a correction and callback 3 still runs and returns one too. The feedback contains both messages, so callback 3 must have run. `seen` shows callback 1 runs on both rounds.
- **Corrections collected in registration order:** The feedback must contain `first correction\nsecond correction`. A reversed order would fail this. Both messages also sort alphabetically in the same order, so a sorting implementation would pass. That is not a plausible reading of the requirement, so I don't count it as a gap.
- **Newline-separated messages in one tool response:** The last user message has exactly one content item, a `ToolResult`. The serialized result contains the `\n`-joined text.
- **Agent asked to resubmit in the same conversation:** The feedback contains `resubmit`. The second request's chat history starts with the first request's history. The next entry is the assistant message. Then comes the tool-result user message.

The case where a callback returns `Err` is outside this requirement, which only applies when all callbacks return `Ok`.
